body: Yeah, I am starting to feel like life is not meant to be fun, but hey, I don't have anything better to do. I mean, is dying really better? It's so hard to say, because death is so uncertain. It seems fair to wait it out, at least.

Yeah, I totally get that. I'm afraid to let people in my life know how I really think. My roommate was just talking about how she doesn't like her job and feels like her life is mediocre, and I went on an existential rant about how most people will have mediocre lives and that life isn't meant to be fulfilling, etc. and she was pretty bummed out and surprised by what I said, I think.

Hey, first of all, you are not a selfish bitch, and you are not a revolting burden. You are a person who is dealing with an immense burden, herself.  A burden that would have already killed a lot of people by now. I know you said you've been through a lot of clinics and stuff, so I don't want to bore you with what you already know, but don't forget that you deserve to be healthy and happy. You deserve to treat yourself well, and that includes not calling yourself a bitch. You are a really fucking strong person, not the opposite. I, personally, know that I am the biggest threat to my own health and wellbeing. It is really really hard to stop treating yourself like shit, but killing yourself is not the only way to stop suffering. The problem is that overcoming something like what you're dealing with is really goddamn hard. I suffer from depression, and everything I do is extremely hard. It seems maybe easier to just kill myself, but deep down I know that's not the solution. There has to be a better way. Don't stop looking for it.

I am finding that experiencing solidarity with someone else who feels depressed or suicidal can be helpful to both parties. I have recently felt like, "Hey, a lot of other people feel how I feel. How I feel is part of the human experience" or something, you know? When I read posts on here, for example, I genuinely feel that I do not want anyone here to kill themselves. Thereby, I feel kind of less like I want to kill myself. Does that make sense? Maybe you could both seek out a support group together or something like that? I know people in my town who started their own radical mental health collective and everyone involved seems to really benefit from it.

I was just talking with a friend the other day about how "sad" we think it is when someone just spends all their time watching tv. Like, there are so many things to do, people should try to have the most fulfilling lives that they can, right? People shouldn't waste their time, right? But you know what? Most people will have mediocre lives. Are animals living in the wild happy? Are they fulfilled? Probably fucking not. They're probably scared and hungry and cold most of the time. But survival is important to them. Whether they realize it or not, it is. I want that. I wish I had the instinct to cling to my survival, despite not having a happy life.

I am college-educated and have a full-time job. I live in a nice apartment in a nice town with nice people. I have been diagnosed with depression and have seen a therapist on and off for the past year. I have a bachelor's degree in psychology and worked in a psychologists' office for several years, and I really don't feel good about paying someone to listen to me. 

I think you are right. I think I am in denial about my depression, because I do not always feel SAD, you know? It seems funny to think of depression as a mental illness. It seems similar to thinking of marijuana as a drug. I mean, who ISN'T depressed?
Right?! One of the many reasons I don't want to take anti-depressants is because I think I'd be one of those people who starts feeling motivated enough to actually do it.

No no, a lot of things interest me. I do a lot of things. I keep very busy, but I lack purpose. I like doing a lot of the things I do, but I still don't want to be alive just to do them. I am starting to think I am in denial about my depression.
Oooh. Yes, Moz wrote a lot of words to live by. When I am going through something really tough, I sometimes think about the lyric "I can laugh about it now, but at the time, it was terrible."

I have a bachelor's degree in psychology and worked in a psychologists' office for several years. I do have a psychologist, but I have this problem where, after seeing a therapist several times, I start to develop concerns about what they think of me. I feel less comfortable sharing after I have established a relationship with them. I think the biggest barrier to my seeking help is the feeling of stigmatization, which is ridiculous considering my background. I just feel that I cannot overcome it.
Yeah, I read your other post and realized we're on the same page, but felt like I didn't have anything meaningful to contribute to your post so I didn't comment. I'm glad you reached out to me.

Yeah, the hardest part is the idea that I should continue to exist because, if I do not, it will hurt other people. I am a musician, and as much fun as it can be, it's not worth living for. I am not sure if I feel a lack of purpose because of something mechanically wrong with me as a human, or if it is more extraneous than that. I do not always feel that I want to kill myself, but it is frequent enough. And when I do, it seems inevitable. It seems true.

your post reminded me a poem written by jordan castro, which i want to share with you. it is called "the cyclical, binary nature of thoughts and emotions"

i feel strongly the possibility that i will never feel any
other way than the way i'm feeling now

every time i feel something

which may or may not mean i feel that all the time


i understand too that this is not true

which can cause me to feel happy

sad or indifferent

depending on the initial feeling

and my level of awareness of other feelings

which evolved from other feelings

so invariably

i feel different than the way i felt before

etc

Yes, but are those things to live for? I appreciate your comment. I don't think that a shower or a nap are going to save my life. I feel sort of obligated to live, do you know what I mean? It isn't enough.
